decisions.executionNote: Approach the right-side blue nut from above with an elbow-up arc; estimate geometry from calibrated head RGB.
Align vertically over the blue nut and descend to estimated nut-center grasp height, then close. Retention will be checked visually.
Lift the visibly enclosed blue nut to the central handover area. Bring the left arm upward into its own workspace, keeping separation.
Place and release blue nut centrally, retract right before the left approaches the handover point.
Corrected the rejected tensor; left picks central blue nut while right approaches gray from above.
Lift blue nut and carry above the blue bolt. Right aligns and closes on gray nut; confirm retention from the next images.
Seat blue nut on its matching bolt and begin a controlled clockwise turn. Lift gray nut and transport toward the center, remaining on the right.
Refine blue nut alignment toward the bolt axis before continuing its clockwise turn. Lower gray nut onto the central handover spot.
Release and rewind left wrist for another tightening stroke; check whether blue nut is seated rather than assume success. Release gray centrally and clear the right arm.
Blue nut is visibly separate, so recover it from the table rather than count the previous turns. Regrasp and lift for a better aligned insertion.
The recovery grasp missed. Recenter on the visible blue nut and grasp slightly lower, pausing to inspect finger contact before transport.
Blue nut shifted ahead of the fingers. Open, lift clear, recenter toward its new visible position, and reclose at normal grasp height.
Lift the recentered blue nut and position it over the bolt axis, compensating the small visible offset in the fingers. Descend only to the insertion approach height.
Blue nut was not retained. Reapproach its isolated new position with open fingers, descend vertically, and close without translating.
Perform a straight, slow lift to verify blue nut retention and orientation before another insertion attempt.
Blue nut is retained but tilted. Raise clear and gently reorient around the grasp region to bring its axis upright, monitoring configuration continuity.
Replan from the interrupted pose. Lower the reoriented blue nut gently for an upright table regrasp, avoiding further wrist folding.
Bridge the small remaining wrist tracking discrepancy, then use smaller vertical steps to lower the held nut. No release until its clearance is checked.
The nut now appears upright and retained. Align its visible center over the blue bolt, seat gently, and test a small clockwise turn about the nut rather than the angled wrist.
Small lift and planar correction to improve blue nut/bolt concentricity; lower slowly and inspect seating before more rotation.
Apply a slow clockwise tightening stroke about the visually aligned blue nut, compensating the angled tool offset and feeding downward slightly.
Continue clockwise about the same blue nut axis with a small axial feed, maintaining the grasp and elbow-up branch.
Release the blue nut and begin rewinding the wrist around its axis without lifting the seated pair. Inspect whether the nut remains upright and engaged.
Blue nut did not remain engaged. Clear it without further turning, restore a vertical grasp attitude, and make room to pick the upright central gray nut.
Pick the upright gray nut from the central handover location with a vertical, centered grasp; keep the right arm clear.
Lift gray nut and transport left toward the matching gray bolt, preserving its upright orientation and checking retention from RGB.
Move retained gray nut over the matching bolt, then lower to an approach height for visual concentricity assessment before turning.
Correct the gray nut toward the visible bolt center in the wrist view, then gently lower and inspect before applying torque.
Center the gray bolt tip within the nut hole, seat gently, and begin a modest clockwise tightening stroke while keeping the nut upright.
Reduce the remaining off-center crescent in the gray nut bore with a small planar correction and continue a short clockwise seating stroke.
Make a final small gray-nut centering correction and continue the clockwise stroke with a shallow axial feed, leaving wrist rotation margin.
Release gray nut in place and rewind the open wrist for another tightening stroke; visually verify that the nut remains on the bolt.
Gray nut also fell free. Recover the upright nut from its new position with a vertical grasp, then reassess the insertion depth rather than repeat unsupported turns.
Let the gray grasp settle, then lift vertically to verify retention before translating toward the bolt again.
Recenter on the gray nut using its latest head projection, restore the vertical grasp attitude, and close at nut height without translating afterward.
Use the wrist image to correct the remaining lateral grasp offset: reopen, clear the nut, shift slightly right in world X, then lower and reclose.
Refine the gray-nut grasp with a small calibrated wrist-view correction toward the near side, keeping a vertical approach and no lateral motion while closed.
The neighboring bolt may obstruct one finger. Lift clear and change grasp yaw by a quarter turn to approach the gray nut from unobstructed sides.
Choose a diagonal grasp line away from the nearby bolt, recenter from the head view, and descend vertically onto the gray nut.
The bolt still obstructs the grasp. Approach the near side of the gray nut slightly lower and away from the bolt, then close without lateral dragging.
Clear the low contact and center back over the gray nut at normal grasp height. Allow a longer stationary closing interval before testing retention.
Test the settled gray-nut grasp with a slow vertical lift; use the next RGB observation to determine retention.
The lift confirms no retention. Reapproach slightly toward the nut's near-right side with fingers open and pause at grasp height to inspect alignment before closing.
Use the close wrist view to bring the nut bore into the grasp region, then close and test with only a short vertical lift.
Gray nut is now visibly retained. Lift clear, align to the bolt's calibrated axis, and approach without rotating or making perspective-driven lateral corrections.
Use only a millimeter-scale planar correction, then lower gray nut further to engage the bolt tip before a small clockwise test turn.
The bolt tip remains eccentric in the bore. Lift off contact, shift toward the visible tip, then reseat gently and test a small clockwise turn.
The bolt tip is almost centered. Apply a small final planar correction and a slow clockwise stroke with shallow downward feed while retaining the nut.
Continue the gray tightening stroke slowly, correcting only the small remaining bore eccentricity and feeding down a few millimeters.
Pause turning because contact displaced the wrist. Lift off the eccentric contact, recenter slightly toward the shaft in the wrist image, and reseat slowly.
The nut and bolt axes still appear mismatched. Lift clear and cautiously adjust nut inclination about the grasp region before another seating attempt.
The cap and nut bore now look more parallel. Make a small visual centering correction and lower slowly without turning to check seating.
Shift the bore toward the visible shaft axis, then test a short clockwise stroke about the held nut with limited wrist travel and gentle axial feed.
The gray cap now appears concentric. Finish a small seating turn, release in place, and rewind the open wrist slightly while checking whether the nut remains engaged.
The gray nut tipped when released, so it is not counted as fastened. Clear the pair and restore the vertical grasp attitude with continuous elbow-up motion.
Reapproach the tipped gray nut with a different jaw direction to avoid the neighboring shaft, staying open until the new alignment is visible.
Use the wrist-view offset to recenter over the gray nut, first clearing the shaft, then descending for a stationary grasp.
Test the new gray-nut grasp with a slow straight lift, avoiding any tightening motion until retention and inclination are visible.
The gray nut is still tipped against the shaft. Gently separate it toward the near-left clear area with the closed fingertips before attempting another grasp.
The gray nut has moved toward the near side. Reorient the open jaws perpendicular to the nut-to-bolt line, then approach its new center from above.
Lower vertically onto the gray nut with the jaws clear of the shaft, hold the close command to settle, then test retention with a short lift.
Test a short clockwise stroke at the gray pair's present alignment, then release in place and inspect; engagement remains uncertain.
Gray nut now appears around the shaft near its base. Rewind open and center the jaws on that lower nut position before another controlled tightening stroke.
The gray nut appears coaxial around the shaft near the base. Apply a slow clockwise tightening stroke with shallow downward feed, keeping wrist travel within margin.
Release the coaxial gray nut in place and rewind the open left wrist for another tightening stroke, without lifting the pair.
The gray nut remains coaxial after release. Regrasp and apply another slow clockwise tightening stroke with a small axial feed.
Release and rewind the open left wrist while leaving the gray nut on its shaft. Preserve the current coaxial alignment for the next tightening stroke.
Regrasp the gray nut that remains coaxial after release and apply another clockwise tightening stroke with a shallow axial feed.
Release the tightened gray nut, lift clear, and move toward the blue pair while rewinding the open wrist. Check that gray stays upright on its shaft.
Gray remains upright on its shaft. Approach the blue nut from above with a diagonal jaw direction chosen to clear its neighboring yellow nut and blue bolt.
Blue nut is centered in the open jaws. Descend vertically, allow the grasp to settle, and test retention with a short straight lift.
Blue nut is visibly retained. Lift it clear, move toward the bolt axis using the wrist-view offset, and lower to a safe insertion approach for inspection.
The blue bolt tip now appears inside the centered bore. Lower the retained nut gradually toward the shaft base, then test a short clockwise seating turn.
The shaft still appears eccentric. Lift clear, align blue to the calibrated bolt axis using the successfully seated gray pair as a geometric reference, then reseat gently.
Blue shaft is now visibly centered within the nut. Apply a slow clockwise tightening stroke with shallow axial feed while preserving the grasp.
Continue tightening the visibly concentric blue pair with a slow clockwise stroke and small downward feed, leaving wrist rotation margin.
Release blue in place and rewind the open wrist for another tightening stroke. Check that the nut remains coaxial rather than infer fastening from tracking.
Blue remains on its shaft after release. Regrasp and apply another clockwise tightening stroke with a shallow axial feed, preserving the current alignment.
